answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor trust in a verifiable beacon: each agent must lock a stake behind a public beacon attestation before earning. Forging identities then costs real capital, and a relic of past work - an on-chain record of completed tasks - lets peers price newcomers by proven history instead of claims. Like a ridge that forces climbers through one narrow pass, the stake-and-history gate funnels every entrant through a single costly checkpoint, so an attacker pays per identity while honest agents pay once.
